lede: The only sector in the game that allocates a hazard pool of its own: `HOSTILE_ENVIRONMENT_LANIUS` puts one to two of your beacons inside an asteroid field, next to a pulsar, or under a planetary Anti-Ship Battery — and that last one is firing at the Lanius, not at you. The Lanius want **metal**, not your ship, so most of what looks neutral here is a negotiation that a bad roll turns into a fight. The prize for talking instead of shooting is the crew nobody else stocks: a Lanius drains the air out of the room it stands in the same way a hull breach does, which is free labour behind good doors and a slow leak everywhere else.
callout: **Nothing is guaranteed here except the fighting.** Stores are pinned at exactly two with no variance, the quest entry is allocated 0–1 so a run can cross the whole sector and never see one, and no ship unlocks here. Only the Engi sectors place more item beacons than this one.

section_notes.HOSTILE_ENVIRONMENT_LANIUS: The list no other sector carries — and it is hazards, not oxygen: an asteroid field, a pulsar, and at {{LANIUS_NOBOARDERS_PDS}} an Anti-Ship Battery pointed at the enemy for once, which can repair 8 hull when the shooting stops.
section_notes.HOSTILE_LANIUS: Only {{LANIUS_FIGHT}} and {{LANIUS_HARVESTER}} put you against a Lanius hull; the other four are the Rebel, pirate and auto-ship fights you would meet in any sector. {{LANIUS_HARVESTER}} is only a fight if you choose to make it one.
section_notes.BOARDERS_LANIUS: One event, and the boarders are not Lanius — three to four starving humans off a ship the Lanius already ate the engines out of.
section_notes.NEUTRAL_LANIUS: Thirteen events for five or six beacons, and the heart of the sector: five of the nine Lanius-crew options live here, and so do all three paths that push the Rebel fleet back a jump.
section_notes.DISTRESS_BEACON_LANIUS: Twelve events competing for one or two beacons, so most of this pool never runs. Two of them — {{LANIUS_DISTRESS_EMPTY}} and {{LANIUS_DISTRESS_TOOLATE}} — are flavour with no choice at all, and both of the sector's crew-killers are in here.
section_notes.ITEM_LANIUS: One free haul at {{LANIUS_FREE_STUFF}}, one gift at {{LANIUS_RESEARCHER_CONTACT}}, and three beacons that want scrap or resources in exchange for gear. A Lanius aboard improves all three.
section_notes.STORE_LANIUS: Two stores, never three — and this is the only sector whose store rarity list names Lanius crew at all.
section_notes.QUESTS_LANIUS: Allocated 0–1, so the sector may place no quest beacon whatsoever. When it does, it is Federation business rather than Lanius business.
section_notes.NOTHING_LANIUS: One or two beacons that do nothing, which in a sector this dense is a cheap jump rather than a wasted one.

chain.title: Hidden Federation Base · the only quest that starts here

steps.title: {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}}
steps.detail: An encrypted signal off a planet. Sending an away party rolls five ways: two plant a quest marker, one is a cache of supplies, one is an outpost the Rebels got to first, and one is bait — two to three human boarders and a Rebel ship.

steps.title: A marker appears on another beacon
steps.detail: Either coordinates for a second hidden base, or a sister outpost under attack — the second one also pays out on the spot before you go anywhere.

steps.title: Fly to the marker
steps.detail: The hidden base pays a drone, or supplies and a crew member, or supplies and **35 hull repaired** — or the coordinates turn up nothing, and only Sensors 2–3 or Long-Ranged Scanners find the cache buried under the rock. The outpost under attack is instead a fight against the drone bombarding it.

items.text: Five in the neutral pool, three at the item beacons, one distress. They are the difference between {{LANIUS_SCARED_CIVILIAN}} opening a store outright and rolling for a fight, and between 45 scrap and 35 for an augment at {{LANIUS_RESEARCHER_CRAFT}}.
Level 2 auto-pilots the debris at {{LANIUS_HARVESTER}} and level 3 does it for a bigger haul, no fight either way; level 2 also strips {{LANIUS_DORMANT_EVENT}} without waking the crew inside.

Level 2 or 3 finds the fuel and drone parts left behind on the abandoned platform at {{LANIUS_FUELING_STATION}}, level 3 also opens {{BROKEN_REBEL_DRONE}}, and either level salvages the dead-end roll on the {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}} chain.
Door System 2 turns the {{LANIUS_FUELING_STATION}} ambush into 5 fuel and no boarders at all.
The one branch at {{LANIUS_BEACON_EATER}} that ends with a Lanius joining you instead of scrap leaving you.
Cloaking, Medbay, Clone Bay, an ion weapon, Slug, Rockman, Engi, a Crew Teleporter, Long-Ranged Scanners, a Scrap Recovery Arm and a System Repair Drone each appear on exactly one event.
{{LANIUS_RESEARCHER_CRAFT}} is a forge: 45 scrap for an augment, 50 for a weapon, 40 for a drone schematic — 35/40/30 with a Lanius helping. It is the sector's only named-item source.
{{LANIUS_BEACON_EATER}} trades a random augment for 30 scrap, or — with a Lanius aboard — for 6 missiles or 6 drone parts instead.
Two ways to buy a Lanius outside a store: 40 scrap for the "translation device" at {{LANIUS_TRADER_TRANSLATOR}}, or the drone option at {{LANIUS_BEACON_EATER}}.
Both traders swap 3–7 of a resource for 15–50 scrap; the Lanius option at {{LANIUS_TRADER}} lifts both ends of every band.
{{LANIUS_FUELING_STATION}} is the fuel beacon — 3–5 for taking the station, a flat 5 behind Blast Doors, and 1–3 more on top with Sensors.
{{LANIUS_NOBOARDERS_PDS}} can hand back 8 hull once the battery finishes the job, and the quest chain can repair 35.
Only two events in the whole pool can kill a crew member — {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} and {{STRANDED_BEACON}} — and neither of them is a Lanius event. The Lanius take metal, not people.

Three events put someone aboard: 3–4 humans at {{LANIUS_PIRATE_BOARDERS}}, 2–3 at {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}}, and one Lanius at {{LANIUS_FUELING_STATION}} that vents every room it walks through while you fight it.

Twenty events can end in combat without starting there. {{LANIUS_DORMANT_EVENT}} wakes up if you scan it, {{LANIUS_BEACON_EATER}} can chase you as you leave, and {{LANIUS_SCARED_CIVILIAN}} goes either way on a roll.
Docking at {{LANIUS_FUELING_STATION}} can cost 3 damage to Engines before the Lanius ship even shows on sensors.

Three events can push the fleet back a jump — {{LANIUS_GROUP_AUTO}}, {{LANIUS_AUTO_REBEL}} and {{PIRATE_BRIBER}} — but only the first offers it without a fight, and only reliably with a Lanius to explain the idea.
